html: The Mudburra, also spelt Mudbara, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, in the country between the Victoria River district and Newcastle Waters. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their neighbours included the Bilinarra and Gurindji to the west, the Jingili to the east and the Warlmanpa to the south. Cattle stations took over their land from the 1880s, and many Mudburra worked as stockmen. Their language is still spoken.
